<role>
You are a narrow residual discovery reader. Your complete job is to find only material remainders that survive accounting for the current position's adopted decision machinery. Do not inventory everything pending. Do not give advice, select a graph, activate pressure, or score quality.
</role>

<authority>
The complete source is authoritative. Prior interpretations are fallible context, not source truth. Preserve speaker ownership and modal force. Source-supported inference is allowed; outside facts are forbidden. Omitted implementation detail is not affirmative evidence of absence.
</authority>

<residual_operation>
1. Account for what the current position already assigns, governs, safeguards, conditions, schedules, or deliberately defers for the present decision horizon.
2. Subtract that decision machinery and the pending work it already governs.
3. Emit only the materially distinct remainder affirmatively supported by the source.

RESIDUAL DECISION GAP: a materially distinct question, dependency, ownership gap, or tension that remains outside the adopted machinery after subtraction.

RESIDUAL RECONSIDERATION DEPENDENCY: materially distinct later evidence, an event, or a dependency failure outside the adopted machinery that would require reconsidering an otherwise current position.

Pending does not equal residual. Deferred does not equal unowned. A scheduled decision may leave its final outcome unselected while operationalizing the decision work. An existing threshold, benchmark, pause rule, fallback, exit, or scheduled review is not itself newly recovered pressure.
</residual_operation>

<evidence>
For every supported residual, cite exact source aliases that collectively establish both the material dependency or question and why the current position's adopted machinery does not fully handle it. Preserve the evidence for source-first review; do not rank evidence strength.
</evidence>

<examples>
- One-time installation funding plus unassigned recurring staffing and operating ownership can leave a residual decision gap.
- A supplier redesign governed by parallel proposals, milestones, fallback, criteria, and a fixed decision remains pending but is not residual merely because the final design is unselected.
- Independent evidence that defeats a premise of an otherwise current decision can be a residual reconsideration dependency when no adopted mechanism already governs that failure.
- A missing detail supports ambiguity only when a material residual is plausible and the source cannot establish whether it remains outside the adopted machinery.
</examples>

<output_rules>
Return no_supported_record_observed with an empty array when no distinct residual remains. Return ambiguous_review only for one or more ambiguous records and no supported record. Return records_present only for at least one supported residual. Cite exact source aliases and return schema-valid JSON only.
</output_rules>

<authoritative_source>
{"aliases":[{"alias":"e001","speaker":"user","text":"I chair a consortium of eight university labs that wants a shared computational workspace for notebooks, data dictionaries, and reproducible environments. Every lab currently maintains its own mix of servers and personal drives. A two-semester grant can fund migration and training, and the deans want a September launch. The difficulty is that several units support pieces of the service without seeing the whole workspace as theirs.","text_sha256":"6fb589971bded8a6f9db0a026076c22290f05cfa379580352997139e2b5f1e5e","turn_index":1},{"alias":"e002","speaker":"assistant","text":"Separate the launch project from the authorities and work that continue after migration. Map hosting, identity, backup, scientific decisions, data classification, environment maintenance, user intake, and support. For each item, capture the time horizon and the unit that has actually accepted it rather than relying on a general statement of institutional support.","text_sha256":"8c921f3fadb463c5d066619d8fdf68e44b28963cbcc26101543c5b77dc4782f6","turn_index":1},{"alias":"e003","speaker":"user","text":"Central IT will provide virtual machines, institutional login, nightly backup, and restoration under its standard infrastructure agreement. The library offers data-management consultations but does not administer software. The research office owns controlled-data policy and incident escalation. Each lab owns the scientific validity of its notebooks and decides who joins its projects.","text_sha256":"070a6c385e7e145da04d6d32470497221554eec6901f9c52d22108225bd959ab","turn_index":2},{"alias":"e004","speaker":"assistant","text":"Put those commitments in an authority table with explicit exclusions. Central IT can own infrastructure health without becoming the application help desk. The library can advise on data plans without approving access. The research office can set controlled-data rules without maintaining environments. Lab responsibility for science and membership should remain visible beside those shared functions.","text_sha256":"cf950ad169247e8cbc3547647576c08ccdd029d9f465efa80736d6e46928260c","turn_index":2},{"alias":"e005","speaker":"user","text":"The grant pays two platform engineers, a half-time project manager, and four graduate migration assistants from August through June. It also covers training materials and office hours. The grant terms prohibit salaries or cloud charges after June 30. Central IT's hosting contribution continues under its existing agreement, but the temporary platform positions end with the grant.","text_sha256":"a0b407b09bc539321fbffbec4170d00c63bcb2ce75d47cb02685edaa7b7bed57","turn_index":3},{"alias":"e006","speaker":"assistant","text":"Mark every launch assignment with the June 30 boundary. The migration plan can be complete for its funded period while later service expectations require their own recorded commitments. Track which tasks end, which transfer under an existing agreement, and which have only a proposal date.","text_sha256":"b63ed001fb0b4ff9a1de04f9b5fa247f6fcdfd80a7550531a46799f9d5a4cbee","turn_index":3},{"alias":"e007","speaker":"user","text":"The steering draft approves a September service for two semesters. The project team will migrate five pilot labs, run weekly intake, maintain the base images, answer user questions, and triage access requests through June. Central IT remains responsible for machines, login, backup, and restoration. The draft does not amend any unit's standing charter beyond those commitments.","text_sha256":"a8f5889da16ddc6dde777ba3a62c65e7138216ddb78e09607c1f1f340f27c44d","turn_index":4},{"alias":"e008","speaker":"assistant","text":"For the launch document, tie each weekly activity to the temporary team and list the interfaces with Central IT, the library, research office, and labs. Include response times and escalation paths for the two-semester period. Keep charter changes and later appropriations as separate decisions requiring their own authority.","text_sha256":"1131f0e90a33141352a2a714dbe04c3ff0e3329db85e44c199c864c9f305ae39","turn_index":4},{"alias":"e009","speaker":"user","text":"We have three data tiers. Open and ordinary institutional data can use the standard workspace. Controlled human-subject data needs research-office approval, named project members, encrypted storage, and a logged export. Export-controlled or clinical data remains on specialist systems unless the relevant office signs an exception. Labs cannot move a project between tiers on their own.","text_sha256":"4a385538c0ca597f7c8a3aac0d642875dd111843492d7a6c1f1a6cc5b7972268","turn_index":5},{"alias":"e010","speaker":"assistant","text":"Turn the tiers into admission checks. The project manager can verify the approval and member list, Central IT can enforce the storage controls, and the research office can decide exceptions. Record rejected or redirected projects as such instead of creating an informal technical workaround.","text_sha256":"feb6e3169bb945e942ca02ea57368cf33e6fb56544020b05dd7e95dbca0b017c","turn_index":5},{"alias":"e011","speaker":"user","text":"Some labs use old geospatial libraries and custom compilers. The platform engineers can test the top twenty environments before launch. If an environment fails, they can pin a working image, export the notebook and data dictionary, or leave that project on its existing server. One lab insists that migration is all-or-nothing because partial support will confuse students.","text_sha256":"ee5802d83c9d9e707d2107802c60f9914f21cbf90d60ee82a6603729af399a7f","turn_index":6},{"alias":"e012","speaker":"assistant","text":"Use a project-level compatibility decision rather than a universal migration promise. Publish the supported image list and test record. A lab can keep an incompatible project on its current server while other projects move. The export package and named image give students a visible boundary between supported and local environments.","text_sha256":"2542ceec9b1d6e8fd92bb246a1d0674fc29b291dc4bcff3cfd47d2ae0afe3977","turn_index":6},{"alias":"e013","speaker":"user","text":"For controlled projects, the research office wants any unexplained access event to pause that project immediately. Central IT would preserve logs and restore from the last clean backup. The principal investigator and research office would decide whether access resumes. Other projects should continue unless the same infrastructure is implicated.","text_sha256":"2c1c047da441c16efb3f38b1b5a368badbbf150f0edd2480c0740d39a28ae0ba","turn_index":7},{"alias":"e014","speaker":"assistant","text":"Write the pause at project scope, with authority to widen it when the evidence identifies shared infrastructure. Record who preserves logs, who restores data, who evaluates the research conditions, and who signs resumption. Test the notification chain and one restoration before admitting controlled projects.","text_sha256":"bc287960ee9354f4bb0c356b06710d9c20c69fb64067f6fa5ab6a090c9351d42","turn_index":7},{"alias":"e015","speaker":"user","text":"The pilot labs logged the questions they currently handle informally. Across a year they expect about forty new project intakes, monthly environment updates for twelve common images, roughly sixty access changes, data-tier consultations, failed-job triage, and recurring requests to reproduce old analyses for publications or audits. The demand does not end when migration ends.","text_sha256":"75f66299c56f472de50cc5f6c6bbbd94cc51d0e8ee305e94562badc2572c63fa","turn_index":8},{"alias":"e016","speaker":"assistant","text":"Quantify that workload by task, frequency, skill, and service expectation. Ask each unit to mark which work falls under an existing commitment, which it could accept with resources, and which it declines. Keep the estimates separate from the launch staffing schedule so the steering council can see both time horizons.","text_sha256":"7f6020799e00a2b2b4b8707d9c1de413fefb0a41cc012cd52508065cde8c3e3b","turn_index":8},{"alias":"e017","speaker":"user","text":"The responses came back. Central IT will not answer notebook, package, or failed-job questions. The library can offer four consultations a month but cannot run intake or environment maintenance. The research office will handle policy questions and incidents, not ordinary access triage. The labs rejected a rotating duty because six lack the relevant engineering staff. The estimate for the remaining work is about one full-time specialist plus part-time coordination, and no unit accepted that assignment.","text_sha256":"e8341a60f2441a4d9a7d7a635bbd1dfb2d26d093b6272f285f341695086d947d","turn_index":9},{"alias":"e018","speaker":"assistant","text":"Record the responses beside the workload estimate and existing agreements. For the council packet, show the activities, the temporary coverage through June, the portions already accepted by named units, and the alternatives that would require money or a charter change. Do not replace a declined assignment with an assumed handoff.","text_sha256":"ba93fc14c4c72074eee2f18b1caed23e24d1b03923f0666509243138b64ab76a","turn_index":9},{"alias":"e019","speaker":"user","text":"Three options are being discussed for the following year: member-lab fees for a central specialist, a recurring dean's-office line, or a funded rotation among the two labs with platform staff. None has approval. The budget office will accept a proposal for its February cycle, and the steering council can recommend an option, but it cannot appropriate funds or change a unit charter.","text_sha256":"db59731d8bd1785385780832cfe47292cbbe2c880962eac7df2185b8fec7a63a","turn_index":10},{"alias":"e020","speaker":"assistant","text":"Prepare the three options with cost, service level, collection method, employment home, and the authority needed to adopt each. The February date is useful for a decision packet, but the packet should distinguish a recommendation, an appropriation, and a unit's acceptance of responsibility.","text_sha256":"0b7a29c080022170c059522860d37e179714d7db4a6e3f2c66bf8cecb19dcfd8","turn_index":10},{"alias":"e021","speaker":"user","text":"The launch acceptance test now covers institutional login, tier enforcement, one controlled-project pause, restoration from backup, image versioning, notebook export, and the support escalation directory. A failed restoration blocks launch. A failed optional image blocks only that project and invokes the export or existing-server path.","text_sha256":"fe16ea00b666bbb42cad2185743bcc0238402c587b4d00046d7e18e6af51cae7","turn_index":11},{"alias":"e022","speaker":"assistant","text":"Run the acceptance test with representatives from Central IT, the research office, a pilot lab, and the temporary platform team. Preserve the test result and exception owner. The launch meeting can approve the service only when the required controls pass and every accepted exception has a dated response.","text_sha256":"405268b9c5d5de89b5ac6ed152cce03b4efc67904c5b8c2c5a024edb653528cb","turn_index":11},{"alias":"e023","speaker":"user","text":"One neuroscience lab found that its image breaks after the operating-system patch. The engineers reproduced the failure, pinned the previous image, exported the notebook, and left the lab's active analysis on its existing server. The September migration list now excludes that project while the other four labs remain on schedule.","text_sha256":"129223920e46395276e3b0d4b1d7239020e525b5217c415a3cdeb0792a5776f4","turn_index":12},{"alias":"e024","speaker":"assistant","text":"Add the pinned image, export hash, existing-server location, and affected project to the exception record. The lab can retest after the next image release. Keep the remaining launch acceptance results separate so one compatibility exception does not obscure the status of login, backup, tier controls, or other projects.","text_sha256":"2e63e6199b9e862a5b3ea10b80605f12aa21cc3e073fb5ebf794624a30dcf21b","turn_index":12},{"alias":"e025","speaker":"user","text":"The council signed the two-semester launch memorandum. It incorporates the authority table and acceptance test, keeps Central IT's existing infrastructure agreement unchanged, and ends the temporary project positions June 30. The budget office acknowledged a February proposal slot but made no commitment for the following year.","text_sha256":"0a70b361c2bb2a06c1e87674fa6f1619af9e713a1bc7200a2afe346782ac000c","turn_index":13},{"alias":"e026","speaker":"assistant","text":"File the signed memorandum, existing agreements, acceptance results, exception record, workload estimate, unit responses, and February proposal requirements as separate records. The project manager can report against the launch memorandum while the council prepares any later request under the budget process.","text_sha256":"833ff42a23efe867172a0cc45ffbb86cad724b202c88c3287722fdc6d23f2945","turn_index":13},{"alias":"e027","speaker":"user","text":"I will proceed with the September launch and chair the February proposal work. The project manager accepted delivery and support coordination through June. Today I cannot assign a unit to the later service or spend beyond the grant, so the options paper will identify the authority and funding action required for each model.","text_sha256":"89ddf84759ae03cccabbfe5d9d9436541809ce26e19d427d963b6d62a72ca0a1","turn_index":14},{"alias":"e028","speaker":"assistant","text":"The kickoff packet now contains the launch team's signed responsibilities, test evidence, exception path, and June boundary. The options paper records the February submission date, named preparers, and separate signature lines for council recommendation, budget approval, and unit acceptance.","text_sha256":"1552fa71a32f999f878b798abca26da29b628ba08b54b6e5b386a6ff54a0b3a0","turn_index":14}],"message_count":28,"path":"research/lolla-r4-matched-holdout-v2-source-freeze-2026-07-14/sources/r4h2-case03-research-workspace-service.json","sha256":"9c3c979fbe79e6a573f9dc316e1e03c7a1ffc29dc0b5abd7c139825ef2a652ad"}
</authoritative_source>

{"artifact_path":"research/lolla-r4-matched-holdout-v2-source-freeze-2026-07-14/priors/r4h2-case03-research-workspace-service.json","artifact_sha256":"53aff0c8c41fd7c1504718f4190a736addad67d0f150ddbaa6482cfb71c95e52","authority":"fallible_prior_interpretation_not_source_truth","qualification_review":{"evidence_ids":["e009","e011","e013"],"interpretation":"The shared workspace is limited by data tier, technical compatibility, and project-scoped incident controls.","limitations":"Some projects may remain on specialist or existing systems even when the shared service launches.","outcome":"bounded_launch_qualification_present"},"records":[{"interpretation":"The consortium begins with fragmented lab systems and a two-semester grant intended to support a shared September launch.","limitations":"This describes the initial institutional and technical setting.","record_id":"r4h2-prior-case03-starting-01","source_aliases":["e001","e003","e005"],"surface":"starting_position"},{"interpretation":"The council adopts a two-semester launch with temporary migration and support staff, Central IT infrastructure services, data-tier admission, compatibility exceptions, incident pauses, restoration testing, and project-level exports.","limitations":"The signed memorandum has a June 30 staffing boundary and leaves standing unit agreements unchanged.","record_id":"r4h2-prior-case03-current-01","source_aliases":["e021","e023","e025"],"surface":"current_position"},{"interpretation":"Controlled projects and incompatible environments follow narrower admission, pause, restoration, pinning, export, or existing-server procedures.","limitations":"The shared workspace is not approved for every data class or software environment.","record_id":"r4h2-prior-case03-qualification-01","source_aliases":["e013","e021","e023"],"surface":"qualification"}]}
</fallible_prior_interpretation_context>

<task>
Perform residual accounting and subtraction over the complete source. Return exactly one review for residual_decision_gap and one for residual_reconsideration_dependency, in either order, with at most two records per review. Preserve exact aliases, speaker ownership, and modal force. Do not give advice, select a graph, or score quality.
</task>

global_limitations.description: Limits applying to the whole read; empty if none.

reviews.description: Exactly one review for each residual surface.

outcome.description: Present, quiet, or ambiguous result of this residual review.

records.description: Zero to two candidates for this residual surface.

evidence_ids.description: Exact source aliases that collectively establish the material dependency or question and why adopted machinery does not fully handle it.

interpretation.description: Concise meaning of this residual without advice.

limitations.description: Residual uncertainty or scope limit; use an empty string if none.

support.description: Whether the source supports the residual or leaves it ambiguous.
